_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When a commit touches that audit's `Code paths` afterwards, the
check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> set
`reviewedAt` to the SHA you reviewed through and say why in `note`.
What is NOT legitimate is bumping `reviewedAt` without reading the diff.
The note is the evidence that someone did.
Both SHAs must survive a squash-merge. A branch SHA resolves in the clone
you wrote it in and nowhere else: CI checks out main plus the PR head, so
the gate that was green on your machine fails for everyone. This has now
cost three fixes (5799e8b, 3ff0c78, defb756). Write the SHA the change
lands on, which for a `reviewedAt` covering the current PR means a
follow-up commit once the squash SHA exists.
Empty since 2026-08-08: all six audits were re-verified and re-anchored,
so every one of them is level with the code. Entries reappear here as
soon as something lands under an audited path — that is the file working,
not the file rotting.

docs/IMAP_SMTP_AUDIT.md.note: 4e3b223 changes which exception MailConnectionProbe throws when the server rejects a login: MailAuthenticationException instead of MailConnectionException, so the reply text stops being rendered into the user-facing error.mail.connectionFailed placeholder and travels as the cause into the log instead. That narrows what server-controlled text reaches the UI; it touches no TLS, auth-mechanism or timeout setting. Re-checked on the probe specifically: pinned ssl.checkserveridentity, the fail-closed OAuth2-requires-SSL guard and the millisecond-string timeouts are all unchanged. Verdict stays PASS.
